questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code counts failed logins for the lockout? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
An attacker sends 50 concurrent requests for an account that is already locked. What does authenticate() do for those requests?
choices: Rejects each with the lock message before invoking the PasswordVerifier
Verifies each password, then rejects them because the account is locked
Queues them until the lock expires
Rejects them with the generic invalid-credentials message

questions.prompt: An unknown username and a known username with a wrong password both produce the same exception message. What is the likely intent?
choices: To keep error handling consistent for logging
To make the lockout counter apply to both cases equally
To stop callers from learning which usernames exist
To avoid calling the PasswordVerifier for unknown users

questions.prompt: The service runs on 4 identical nodes behind a round-robin load balancer, each with its own LoginThrottle. What is the consequence for the lockout policy?
choices: Locks are shared automatically because the maps are ConcurrentHashMaps
Successful logins on one node clear failures on all nodes
A user's failures are counted per node, so an attacker can make roughly four times maxFailures attempts before every node locks
